limitations: Chromium explicitly uses SwiftShader; Firefox default headless uses a different backend. Neither establishes physical GPU/controller performance.
RAF callback intervals are browser pacing, not GPU completion or display scanout. CPU buckets are rolling samples and do not cover all main-thread work. Firefox clocks are coarse.
Short repeated samples show variance; no stable 60 FPS or universal HUD speedup claim. Before/after camera and presentation differ; use isolated component sweep for causal checks.
Virtual injection-to-observed-skill-start is not physical latency or damage latency.

chromium-main.method: 6s windows after 2s warmup; main: three interleaved repeats, 5/10/20/30 enemies, before legacy pre-299 containment and after full polish with diagnostics open. Effects: two repeats. Same 1920x1080 viewport/balanced 960x540, durable enemies/immortal player, muted, virtual Xbox primary every 700ms. Different presentation composition in before/after; only hudBefore/hudAfter isolates containment.

chromium.method: 6s after 2s warmup per paired legacy/skill encounter, immortal player, durable 60000HP enemies to hold entity counts, virtual Xbox primary edge every 700ms aimed away from enemies. Injection-to-observed-skill-start latency measured separately from HUD request-to-start metric. No native hardware latency claim. CPU metrics are rolling p95; ability metric includes combat. Effects count is concurrent statuses and projectiles, not cumulative events.
